minutes.headline: FY25 school budget surplus of roughly $600K traced largely to a grant line double-budgeted, unspent
minutes.summary: The School Committee reviewed a reconciled FY25 budget surplus, with the business manager and superintendent explaining it stemmed mainly from a paraprofessional line double-budgeted against a grant plus general underspending on maintenance, custodial and instructional lines, none of which affected the separate cuts made for FY26. Extensive public and committee questioning pressed on accountability, Munis reporting reliability, and the need for regular budget-to-actual reporting and backup support for the business manager going forward. The committee also worked through a draft FY27 capital plan, debating how to finance a needed turf field/track replacement alongside a possible solar revenue project, and took votes on line-item transfers, a music program donation, a grant application, new legal counsel, and added secretarial hours at the high school.

what_happened.line: The business manager reported a reconciled FY25 school budget surplus, attributed mainly to a paraprofessional line double-budgeted against a grant plus underspending on maintenance, custodial and instructional lines.
Officials said the surplus did not affect the separate cuts already made to the FY26 budget.
The committee replaced a generator with the turf field/track project on the draft FY27 capital plan priority list, to be sent to the capital planning committee by October 1.
The business office agreed to start monthly budget-to-actual reporting to the committee after residents said prior requests for such reports had gone unanswered.
The committee also passed routine items: four line-item transfers, a music-boosters donation, a state arts grant application, new legal counsel, and added secretarial hours at the high school.

why_it_matters: The surplus explanation and the new monthly budget-to-actual reports speak to how closely residents can track whether school spending matches what was voted, not to who was at fault for the earlier mismatch.

The turf field/track project's move onto the capital plan, financed through borrowing, is a future debt-service item that would show up in the town's capital budget and tax bills once financing is worked out.
The added secretarial hours and legal counsel change are funded from existing lines and do not appear to require new town money.
